The power of an original idea: Creating what matters in the age of AI

Adobe's recap of the session, by Resh Sidhu.

Read on Adobe

Twenty years ago, I taught Photoshop on computers so old you could hear them thinking. On November 11, 2026, I stepped onto the Discovery Stage at Adobe MAX to share what I had learned. It felt like a full-circle moment.

The eight-minute talk was part of a TED-style customer series created by Rani Mani of Adobe and hosted by Resh Sidhu. Each speaker responded to one question: if everyone can create, who will create what matters? I shared the stage with Minjin Kang of Microsoft and Phillip Kauffman of Monster Energy.

At the center was a simple belief: AI brings speed. People bring creativity and judgment. I shared how seven years of creative transformation at Lumen taught us to help creatives learn together, build repeatable systems and protect the human decisions that make the work matter.

My mentor, Moria Fredrickson, had spoken at Adobe MAX and Adobe Summit. She believed in my work, advocated for me and helped make this moment possible.

"She's warm, engaging and an excellent speaker... A full on rising star in this space."Moria Fredrickson, in her nomination to Adobe.

I also built this page with Copilot, working through the copy, color, typography, UX and layout until it felt like mine. It was a small example of the talk's point: the tool helped me move faster, but human judgment still shaped the result.

The systems mattered, but the point was never the tools. It was how we make room for creativity, shared standards and responsible decisions while AI accelerates the work.

"Giving people space to learn together, test ideas, and establish shared standards helps teams scale their judgment."Resh Sidhu, VP, Creative at Adobe, in her recap.

Afterward, a line of people waited to talk. I sent so many copies of the presentation that I put the talk, prompts and practical takeaways here.

AI brings speed. People bring judgment.

Prompt recipes.

A good prompt is a set of blocks you can change deliberately. Pick a recipe, then change one block at a time.

ImageSee formula
+++

Tap a block to see what it controls.

Stylized layered mountain forms representing a team climbing toward a shared goal, linked by winding trails. Bold, high-contrast, flat vector or cut-paper collage style with crisp shapes and clean edges. Bright, sparse negative space. Limit color palette to two or three of your brand colors.

Video B-rollSee formula
+++

Tap a block to see what it controls.

Modern broadcast control room with seafoam and white accents. A broadcast technician transfers large sports media files to a live TV feed. Bright natural lighting, eye-level static shot. Minimal overlays, focused collaborative mood.

VoiceoverSee formula
+++

Tap a block to see what it controls.

A warm, confident narrator in her 30s. Friendly and conversational, like talking to a colleague. Steady medium pace with natural pauses. Clean studio sound, no background noise.

Sound effectsSee formula
+++

Tap a block to see what it controls.

Soft whoosh with a light digital shimmer. A card slides onto the screen. Close and crisp, small room, no echo. Under 2 seconds.

MusicSee formula
+++

Tap a block to see what it controls.

Modern pop-electronic. Uplifting and forward-moving. Warm piano, light synth pads, soft percussion at 100 BPM. 30 seconds, gentle build, clean ending. Instrumental, no vocals.
